Named in the patent but never drawn. Structure from input/structures-curated.json. 3-oxobutanenitrile. Named as the step 8 additive by all three written tellings of the route, and the compound [0004] says the invention eliminated, calling it highly toxic. Curated because the patent never draws it. IT IS ONE HALF OF THE PAIR A REVIEWER IS ASKED TO TELL APART: claims CN104292137A_p02_x3 and CN104292137A_p05_x3 ask whether step 8 means this or acetone cyanohydrin, which the drawn scheme shows instead. The two are distinguishable by name only to a chemist, and trivially by eye once both are drawn: this one is a straight three-carbon chain carrying a ketone, the other is branched at a quaternary carbon carrying an OH. The entry exists so the reviewer can settle the question by looking rather than by trusting a name.

The identifier string is itself a SMILES, read off the drawn scheme. 2,6-dichlorotoluene. The gold record carries this SMILES AS its identifier (identifier_type smiles), so it resolves as patent_scheme. It is the starting material of the DRAWN scheme, which is a different route from the prose: the prose starts from 2-chlorotoluene. All 9 drawn records carry validation_flag route_attribution_unclear.

The identifier string is itself a SMILES, read off the drawn scheme. Product of drawn scheme step 2. Oxidised to the sulfone at scheme step 3, which is where the drawn route rejoins the prose route.

Named in the patent but never drawn. Structure from input/structures-curated.json. 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile. What the drawn scheme shows above the step 8 arrow, drawn as a structure rather than written: a quaternary carbon bearing CN, OH and two methyls. Curated because it is drawn but never named in the text, so gold/structures.json does not carry it under this identifier. THE OTHER HALF OF THE PAIR: see the note on cyanoacetone. Drawing both is the whole point, because the comparison is the evidence and neither drawing settles the question on its own.
